memory_lessons.applicability: Use as context for another topology comparison, not as a per-kernel performance conclusion.
memory_lessons.claim: The preceding distinct T1 program was correct on all 10 reported cases and measured 4.42078e-05 seconds across three samples; baseline measured 4.64832e-05 seconds across three samples. These whole-call results alone do not establish which transformation caused the difference.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare this 256-partial cap against the previous 1024-partial cap using compatible repeated full-call measurements, including the 65,536-element case.

proposal.hypothesis: The only prior distinct T1 candidate (d35c915c07694ddb) was valid at 4.42078e-05 seconds over three samples, versus the baseline's 4.64832e-05 seconds over three samples; these whole-call results do not isolate the cause. That candidate finalized up to 1024 partials in one CTA. This variant keeps the 128-thread reduction tree and 128-input first-stage tile fixed, but lowers the finalizer cap to 256. It tests whether parallelizing intermediate counts such as 512 partials offsets the added launch. At n=4,194,304, the expected hierarchy still reduces 32,768 initial partials to 256 before finalization. No speedup is assumed.

retained: Kept the 128-thread modulo/shared-memory reduction tree for the input partial kernel and all parallel partial-reduction stages.
Accumulate input and intermediate partials as int64; narrow only when the exact total is written to the int output.
Lowered the one-CTA finalization cap to 256 partials; counts above the cap go through parallel 128-way reduction stages.
Use two packed scratch buffers sized by the initial partial count, alternate stage outputs, and write the final result directly to out.
Handle n == 0 as a zero sum and reject invalid n or required null pointers without relying on scratch initialization.
